title: Fan Zhendong returns after seven weeks and stays unbeaten in the Bundesliga for Borussia Düsseldorf
seo_title: Fan Zhendong returns, still unbeaten for Düsseldorf
description: Fan Zhendong won his first match in seven weeks for Borussia Düsseldorf and is eight from eight in the Bundesliga, away from the world tour.
standfirst: The Olympic champion, out of the world rankings since 2024, lost eight points against Grünwettersbach. His contract runs out in the summer, and his old club Saarbrücken are next.
body: Fan Zhendong played his first match for Borussia Düsseldorf in seven weeks on Sunday, beating Adrian Gossow of ASC Grünwettersbach 11-2, 11-3, 11-3 to keep his perfect record in the Tischtennis Bundesliga this season.

The Olympic champion and former world No 1 has now won all eight of his league singles for Düsseldorf, dropping three games in total. The club beat a weakened Grünwettersbach 3-0 without losing a game in front of a sell-out crowd of 1,100 at the ARAG CenterCourt. It was their eighth win in eight matches, and they lead the table with 16 points from 16.
## Seven weeks out of the team

Fan's previous match was on 27 September, when he beat Borussia Dortmund's Joao Geraldo 13-11, 12-10, 11-9 and Wim Verdonschot in four games. Düsseldorf then had no league match for six weeks, and when they returned Fan was left out of the team that won 3-2 at TTC Grenzau on 9 November and of the side that [beat AS Pontoise-Cergy 3-1](/news/ettu-champions-league-men-2026-27-last-16-pontoise-dusseldorf.html) in the first leg of their Champions League last-16 tie three days later.

The club has not given a reason. Some Chinese outlets have described it as rotation, and none has reported an injury. There was little sign of rust on Sunday: Gossow, 18, who normally plays for Grünwettersbach's second team in the third division, won eight points in three games.

Danny Heister, Düsseldorf's head coach, was pleased with how his squad had handled the run of matches. "Despite the strain of three matches in the Bundesliga and the Champions League and the trip to France, we got through all the games well," he said (translated from German).
## Why he is missing from the world rankings

Fan, 29, has not played on the World Table Tennis circuit since December 2024, when he and Chen Meng, the two Olympic singles champions, [withdrew from the world rankings](/news/wtt-calendar-player-workload-injuries.html) rather than accept WTT's fines for players who miss its events. With no ranking points, he does not appear in the [world rankings](/rankings.html), so his matches in Germany are the clearest guide to his form.

So far the numbers are as good as ever. Last season, his only one at 1. FC Saarbrücken, he won 21 of his 24 regular-season Bundesliga singles and helped the club to a treble of the German Cup, the Champions League and the German title, beating Düsseldorf in the Final4 final in Frankfurt. Two of those three defeats came on the opening day, against TTC Bergneustadt's Romain Ruiz and Benedikt Duda. When he met them again in September, he beat both 3-0.

Fan joined Düsseldorf in July on a one-year contract, and his next move is undecided. Andreas Preuß, the club's manager, said this month that no player or coach has a contract beyond this season, that talks would begin in November and that he does not expect quick decisions. "A lot is open when it comes to squad planning," he said (translated from German), adding that he would naturally speak to Fan.

The club's interest is not only sporting. Preuß said Fan's arrival had changed everything from ticketing to social media, and Düsseldorf's matches are now shown live in more than 300 cinemas in China. [Read more on the contract talks](/news/borussia-dusseldorf-fan-zhendong-contracts-2026.html), and on [why the world's best players still choose the Bundesliga](/news/why-best-table-tennis-players-play-in-germany-bundesliga.html).

His next match is against his old club. Düsseldorf play 1. FC Saarbrücken, in Trier, on Sunday 22 November at 2.30pm UK time, in what the club calls the league's top game. Saarbrücken lost the first leg of their own Champions League last-16 tie 3-2 at Lille. Düsseldorf's second leg against Pontoise-Cergy is at home on 18 December.
